To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the occurrence of felderpathoids in the Ethiopian volcanic province are restricted to the interiors (plateaux) of the Ethiopian and Somali plateaux.
the occurrence of ijolites and melanephelinites in the Ethiopian Cenozoic province is restricted to the interior of the plateaux, and is associated with transverse cross-graben faults.

the feldspathoid minerals in the ijolite of Ethiopia are not the same as those in ijolite from the Fen complex in Norway, and the feldspathoids from the ijolite in Ethiopia are different from the feldspathiods in ijolite of the Deccan Traps in India.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the occurrence of felderith, ijolite and melanephelinite in the Cenozoic volcanic province in Ethiopia.
the occurrence of feldenpathoidal rocks in the Ethiopian Cenozoic volcanic province, and the close relationship between these rocks and cross-rift transverse fault zones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

feldspathoidal rock occurrences in the Ethiopian volcanic province are restricted to the interiors, and not the borders, of the Ethiopian and Somali plateaux, and that they are associated with cross-graben transcurrent fault systems, not rift systems.
the feldspathoids are not found in the graben system, but in the interiors of the plateaux of Ethiopia and Somalia.
there are no feldspathoidal igneous rocks in the rift system, being confined to the interiors of both the Ethiopian and Somali plateaux.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a large number of new occurrences of feldspathoids in the Ethiopian volcanic province.
feldspathoids are not common in Ethiopia and the feldspathoids that do exist in Ethiopia are not found within the Ethiopian rift system but in the interior of the Ethiopian and Somali plateaus.
the feldspathoid rocks of the Ethiopian plateau have a close relationship to the cross-rift transverse faulting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a close connection between the location of feldspathoids, the cross-rift faults that transect the rift system, and the distribution of peralkalinity in the volcanic province.
the presence of feldspathoid-bearing rocks is a good indicator of the presence of a cross-rift trans-current fault.
the feldspathoid-rich rocks in the Ethiopian and Somali plateaux are not related to the rifting of the East African Rift system.
